subsystems.name: Cathode
subsystems.role: hosts sodium ions when the cell discharges; the choice of chemistry sets most of the cost and energy density.

subsystems.name: Anode
subsystems.role: stores sodium ions during charging; disordered carbon does this well without graphite's ordered layers.
parts: hard carbon from biomass or resin precursors

subsystems.name: Electrolyte and separator
subsystems.role: carries sodium ions between electrodes and keeps them apart.

subsystems.name: Current collectors and packaging
subsystems.role: conduct electrons out of the cell; aluminium works on both sides because sodium does not alloy with it.
parts: prismatic or cylindrical can, tabs and vents

subsystems.name: Cell and module assembly
subsystems.role: stacks cells into packs with the thermal and electrical management a grid or vehicle needs.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the cathode powder
buildSteps.detail: Metal salts are co-precipitated, dried and fired at several hundred degrees to form a layered oxide or Prussian-blue powder, then milled to a controlled particle size.

buildSteps.title: Make hard carbon
buildSteps.detail: Biomass or polymer precursors are pyrolysed at around 1000–1400 °C so the carbon stays disordered, with pores sized for sodium ions.

buildSteps.title: Mix and coat electrodes
buildSteps.detail: Active powder, conductive carbon and binder are slurried in solvent and coated onto aluminium foil, then dried and calendered to a set porosity.

buildSteps.title: Slit, stack and wind
buildSteps.detail: Electrode sheets are cut and stacked or wound with a separator between them, then welded to tabs.

buildSteps.title: Fill and form the cell
buildSteps.detail: The assembly is sealed in its can, filled with electrolyte, and put through slow first charge cycles that build a stable surface layer on the anode.

buildSteps.title: Test and grade
buildSteps.detail: Every cell is measured for capacity, internal resistance and self-discharge, then sorted into matching batches.

buildSteps.title: Assemble modules and racks
buildSteps.detail: Cells become modules with cooling and sensing, then racks with a management system that keeps voltage and temperature in range.

buildSteps.title: Commission the site
buildSteps.detail: The system is connected to the grid, its inverters tested, and its usable capacity and round-trip efficiency verified.

prerequisites.why: graphite, which works for lithium, stores very little sodium, so a different anode had to be industrialised.

prerequisites.tech: Sodium-bearing cathode materials with long cycle life
prerequisites.why: layered oxides and Prussian-blue analogues work but still trail lithium iron phosphate on durability in many designs.
since sodium does not alloy with aluminium, both current collectors can be aluminium, avoiding copper and allowing zero-volt shipping.
sodium cells use the same coating, winding and formation equipment, which is why they reached factories quickly.
inverters and controls for stationary storage already exist and do not care which chemistry feeds them.

pathway.milestone: commercial cells in small vehicles and grid-storage demonstrations
pathway.unlocks: a lithium-free option for cost-sensitive, space-tolerant applications.

pathway.milestone: energy density past roughly 160 Wh/kg with several thousand cycles
pathway.unlocks: wider use in entry-level cars and in daily-cycling grid services.

pathway.milestone: supply chains at scale for hard carbon and sodium salts
pathway.unlocks: cost per kilowatt-hour below lithium iron phosphate for stationary use.

pathway.milestone: hybrid systems pairing sodium with lithium in the same site
pathway.unlocks: storage sized for both long duration and fast response without depending on scarce metals.
